name: Pitch Play
description: One sample or many, played chromatically on the pads and from a MIDI keyboard
changelog: 0.10.3: the sequencer's presses are the kit's notes and the kit plays them -- a song playing under this screen came out as its Drums track's notes on the instrument.

0.10.2: the instrument already up -- the song's, or its Pitch track's in Arrange -- is the one the screen shows and EDIT changes. It said "Pick a sample" over the song's instrument, EDIT began a new one, and the last one shown here was built again in the song's place.

0.10.1: an instrument with a file of its own keeps what EDIT changed in it -- saved to that file once the edit plays, as a kit keeps its edits. A song names the file, and opening it again played the preset as it was before the edit.

0.10.0: CHORD opens the Chord Designer (core 2.2 crosspad::chords) in place of the chord types, the Diatonic and Types modes and the degree progressions: up to sixteen chords spelled out -- root on C..B and #, maj min 7 maj7 m7 9 m9 13 dim sus4, INV, ADD, DEL, MOVE -- twelve genre presets (FUNK .. POP, INIT), VOICE close/open/wide, and pad n plays chord n in the octave OCT says, the pads past the list silent. A key acts on press and plays the chord for 900 ms; a pad selects the chord it plays; ON/OFF gives the pads back their notes. The list is kept in NVS. A held chord is five notes now (the ninths and the 13). The SCALE window is the key, the scale and the transpose. An instrument the kit browser's PITCH list picks is the one it opens (core instrumentOpenRequest()). Requires core 2.2.

0.9.1: builds on core 1.70+/gui 1.28+ and on core/gui 2.x (>=1.70.0,<3.0.0 and >=1.28.0,<3.0.0) for the merge window; a root deleted before the app's teardown is handled (gui 2.0 calls destroy with none)

0.9.0: on an Arrange Pitch track's screen PLAY, REC and DUB are the arrangement's (core 1.58 songTransport()): REC records what these keys play onto the track from Arrange's playhead, as a block of its own notes, the same as REC in Arrange -- it used to play the song from bar one and record into the track's scene. Requires core 1.58.
0.8.0: on an Arrange Pitch track's screen the first key is SEQ: the track's notes in the sequencer's seq view, whose EDIT comes back here. SCALE stays the field at the top.

0.7.0: opened by Arrange for a Pitch track, this screen is that track's: it takes the transport for the track's scene laid on the song, so PLAY plays the arrangement and REC / DUB record what the keys play. Opened from MODE it is as before.

0.6.0: a held note out of one sample -- EDIT gives each zone a START (the attack, played once) apart from its loop, and XF, a crossfade from the loop's end into what leads up to its start, so the wrap has no seam; LOOP ON now lands past the attack with a quarter of the loop crossfaded. The fifth key is EDIT > and opens the zones directly; SAMPLE > was a second door to the window the instrument's name opens, which keeps the card, the takes and SAVE. EDIT's values -- ROOT, S, E, START, XF -- are fields turned with the encoder (a click starts turning, a click stops; faster the faster it turns) instead of a - and a + beside each. The zone's waveform is drawn again, in the right panel and under the loop in EDIT with the loop, the crossfade and the start marked -- it had been asked of the tools by its logical path, which opens nothing, and asked again every tick. Needs core 1.55 (Zone::start, Zone::loopXfade).

0.5.0: the scale as a shape -- a chromatic octave in the SCALE window, the pitch classes a pad actually sounds lit and the key ringed; and LOOP in EDIT -- start and end per zone, shown as seconds with the region drawn over the sample. Needs core 1.48 (IInstrumentHost::zoneAudio).

0.4.1: notes are spelled the way the key spells them -- Eb, Bb, Ab and Db in the six flat keys, sharps elsewhere. A progression written in Eb reading "D#" on the pads was the right sound on the wrong piece of paper.

0.4.0: forty-six progressions through core 1.45 -- the thirty jazz, soul, lo-fi and trap ones included -- and picking one now brings its mode with it, so Backdoor arrives in Mixolydian and Lydian Dream in Lydian instead of being read as degrees of whatever was selected.

0.3.1: the chord list follows core 1.44 -- ninth chords and eight R&B/soul progressions (Soul Turn, ii-V-I, Gospel, Deceptive, Minor Soul, Tritone, Neo-Soul, Soul Shuffle). The editor cycles chord types by MusicTheory::playableChordCount() rather than a literal twelve.

0.3.0: the music comes from crosspad::MusicTheory instead of this file -- nine scales, fourteen chord types (Diatonic among them, which takes its quality from the degree) and eight progressions, none of which was reachable before because nothing linked it. SCALE picks key, scale, transpose and chord; "Own progression" edits up to eight progressions of your own, steps of (degree, chord), kept in NVS across a reboot and playing the moment they are saved. Requires core 1.42.

0.2.0: key, scale, transpose and chords. The pads are sixteen degrees of a scale from a key (chromatic, major, minor, dorian, mixolydian, two pentatonics, blues, harmonic minor) shifted by a transpose of -12..+12; a pad can play a power chord, a triad, a 7th or an octave, built from the scale so it stays in key -- and from fixed intervals on chromatic, where two degrees is a whole tone. SCALE on the top row opens the window and carries the answer ("C maj"); a dot marks chords on.

0.1.0: an instrument from one sample or many, picked from a drop-down (saved instruments, the Recorder's takes, the whole card); the pads play it chromatically from a base note, OCT moves it, a MIDI keyboard plays it too; EDIT lists the zones -- add one from the card, remove one, set its root or leave it to detection; SAVE keeps it in /crosspad/pitchplay with its samples copied in; the engine is borrowed from the kits while the app is open (core 1.38 IInstrumentHost); requires core 1.38 and gui 1.18
